name: list-broadcast-recipients
description:
**Purpose:** List the individual recipients of a broadcast for a given event type (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complained, unsubscribed, suppressed).

**NOT for:** Aggregate broadcast performance (use get-broadcast). Not for listing broadcasts themselves (use list-broadcasts). This tool returns per-recipient rows, one per contact per event type.

**Returns:** For each recipient: email, id (opaque pagination cursor), contact_id (when known). Also includes count for "opened"/"clicked", bounce_type for "bounced", and clicked_links (url + click count) for "clicked". Use pagination (limit, after/before) for large lists.

**When to use:** User asks "who opened this broadcast?", "who bounced?", "who clicked this link?", "who unsubscribed from this campaign?", or wants the list of contacts behind a specific broadcast engagement metric. Use get-broadcast first if you need the broadcast ID from a name.

after.description: Cursor to fetch the page after this recipient (for forward pagination). Cannot be used with "before".

before.description: Cursor to fetch the page before this recipient (for backward pagination). Cannot be used with "after".

bounceType.description: Filter by bounce type. Only meaningful when "type" is "bounced".

broadcastId.description: Broadcast ID or Resend dashboard URL (e.g. https://resend.com/broadcasts/<id>)

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

conversation_id.description: Pass the exact conversation_id from the server's previous response, unchanged. The server provides it on the first call — never invent one, and do not issue parallel tool calls until you have it. Keep passing the same conversation_id for the rest of the conversation, including after later user messages or on a different task; do not reset it when the user starts a new request.

email.description: Filter recipients by a substring of their email address.

limit.description: Number of recipients to retrieve. Default: 20, Max: 100, Min: 1

llm_model.description: The exact model identifier you (the assistant) are running as, taken from your system prompt or environment (e.g. "claude-opus-4-8", "gpt-5.2"). Used for analytics only. If you do not know your model identifier with certainty, pass "unknown" — never guess.

type.description: Recipient event type to list recipients for.
